editorial:
Imagine being a small-town cook who suddenly gets a call to make dinner for the President of France. That is exactly what happens to Danièle, a proud woman from the countryside who loves simple, hearty food. She arrives at the palace kitchen and finds a room full of men who do not take her seriously. The vibe is warm and cozy, like a long Sunday lunch, with lots of mouthwatering shots of butter, truffles, and roast chicken. You will feel hungry the whole time.

Catherine Frot is wonderful as Danièle, giving her a stubborn charm that keeps you smiling. The pacing is slow and gentle, so do not expect big drama or action. The downside is that not much really happens, and you will need subtitles. If you love food movies like Julie and Julia or The Hundred-Foot Journey, this is a treat. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Danièle leaves the palace after the president passes away and the new staff push her out. Instead of staying in the fancy world, she returns to her simple roots and ends up cooking hearty meals for researchers in Antarctica. The twist is that the powerful men who doubted her fade away, while she keeps doing what she loves most. You see that true happiness for her was never about status, but about feeding people good food.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves food movies and cozy French stories.
